verses.pali: Atha kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then the brahmin Jānussoṇi went up to the Buddha, and exchanged greetings with him. Seated to one side he said to the Buddha:
“‘All exists’: this is one extreme, brahmin.”

verses.pali: “‘Sabbaṁ natthī’ti kho, brāhmaṇa, ayaṁ dutiyo anto.
verses.english: “‘All does not exist’: this is the second extreme.

verses.pali: Ete te, brāhmaṇa, ubho ante anupagamma majjhena tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti:
verses.english: Avoiding these two extremes, the Realized One teaches by the middle way:
Choices are a requirement for consciousness. …
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.
When ignorance fades away and ceases with no residue left behind, choices cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’”

verses.pali: Evaṁ vutte, jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: When he said this, the brahmin Jānussoṇi said to the Buddha,
From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.”
